title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
An AI agent deployed to automatically triage GitHub issues was given excessive permissions and no human review step. The agent could be manipulated through prompt injection in issue titles to execute arbitrary code, steal publishing credentials, and publish malicious packages to millions of developers. This failure combined a system deployed without adequate access controls, insufficient human oversight in the approval chain, and the use of an AI system in a high-privilege context where it was never meant to operate independently.

The vulnerability existed from late December 2025 through February 9, 2026. A researcher discovered the flaw and reported it starting January 1st, but received no response until the issue was publicly disclosed, when the maintainers fixed it within an hour by removing the workflow and rotating credentials. Whether an actual attack succeeded or was merely attempted is not established by the reporting.

summary:
# Summary

Cline, an open-source AI coding tool used by millions of developers, had a critical security vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow from late December 2025 through February 9, 2026. The issue stemmed from an AI agent designed to automatically triage GitHub issues that was configured with excessive privileges and could be manipulated through prompt injection attacks. By crafting a malicious issue title, an attacker could trick the AI into executing arbitrary code and installing malicious packages.

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability through a technique called cache poisoning to steal publishing credentials and distribute malware to millions of developers across the VS Code Marketplace, OpenVSX, and NPM. Evidence suggests someone attempted to exploit the flaw, though no malicious updates were successfully released. The researcher who discovered the vulnerability repeatedly tried to contact Cline's team starting January 1st but received no response until publicly disclosing the issue on February 9th, 2026. Cline fixed the problem within an hour of public disclosure by removing the vulnerable workflow and rotating credentials.
